transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I just don’t feel like doing any of the things I used to love anymore, even painting or going to my dance class. Everything just feels so heavy and empty now, and I can't seem to find the energy to care about them.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you ever experienced similar periods of low mood in the past?

It's been going on for about four months now, ever since my youngest daughter moved away and the community center cut back the arts programs. I have never felt anything like this before in my entire life; this is completely new to me.
Have you ever experienced periods in your life where you felt the opposite—unusually energetic, highly active, or like you needed much less sleep than usual?
No, I've never had times like that at all. I have always been very steady, and I've never experienced periods of feeling hyperactive or needing less sleep.
How has your sleep been during these past four months—are you having trouble sleeping, or perhaps sleeping much more than usual?
I'm not really sure, to be honest, as I haven't paid much attention to my sleep lately. I just know that I feel constantly exhausted and tired during the day, no matter what.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight since you started feeling this way?
I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite or my weight since all of this started. I'm not really sure if anything has shifted there.
Along with feeling heavy and empty, have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, perhaps blaming yourself for things?

Yes, I feel like a completely useless burden to my family, and I'm convinced my kids only call me out of pity. I also keep thinking that the community center cutbacks and everyone drifting away is somehow my fault, like I must have done something wrong.
Have you found it harder than usual to concentrate, focus on daily tasks, or make decisions since these feelings started?
I haven't really noticed any specific trouble with concentrating or making decisions. It's more that I just feel too exhausted and slow to even try doing much of anything in the first place.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself, or felt like life is no longer worth living?

Sometimes I do think it would just be easier for everyone if I didn't wake up in the morning. I've even found myself picturing taking all of my blood pressure pills at once, though I haven't actually done anything to hurt myself.
To help me understand your physical health better, have you ever been diagnosed with any thyroid problems, or started any new medications recently besides your blood pressure pills?
No, I don't have any known thyroid issues, and I haven't started any new medications recently. I only take my usual blood pressure pills that I've been on for a while.
Have you noticed if your low mood or lack of energy feels worse at any specific time of the day, such as when you first wake up in the morning?

Yes, mornings are definitely the hardest time for me. I wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest, like both my house and my heart are completely hollow, and I often end up just sitting and crying over nothing in particular.
Have you recently heard voices or seen things that others couldn't, or felt strongly convinced of things that other people tell you are not real?

Yes, sometimes when the house is quiet, I hear my daughter's voice in the hallway saying they'd be better off without me and that I just drag everyone down, even though she lives hours away and my husband says no one is there. I've also become deeply convinced my family is planning to abandon me because I'm a burden, though everyone tells me that isn't true. These voices and thoughts only started happening after this heavy sadness took hold a few months ago.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe depressive episode characterized by a four-month history of profound anhedonia, constant fatigue, feelings of worthlessness and excessive guilt, and active suicidal ideation. Additionally, she exhibits mood-congruent psychotic features, including auditory hallucinations (hearing her daughter's voice saying they would be better off without her) and persecutory/somatic delusions (believing her family plans to abandon her because she is a burden). There is no history of manic or hypomanic episodes, and the symptoms are not attributable to substance use or a general medical condition, meeting the criteria for a Severe Depressive Episode with Psychotic Symptoms (F32.3).
